title: Obsidian Graph Stats Streak Gap Alert
dataSources: Obsidian graph stats (`obsidian:stats`), Roam daily notes (`roam:daily`), Logseq tasks (`logseq:task`), Zettelkasten notes (`zettel:note`), PKM review summaries (`pkm:review`).
app: Obsidian graph stats, Roam daily notes, Logseq task exports, and Zettelkasten counts streamed to Splunk HEC via plugins, CSV exports, and scripted vault scans.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats
| stats latest(streak_days) as streak_days, max(_time) as last_seen by user
| eval days_since=round((now()-last_seen)/86400,1)
| where days_since>2
| sort - days_since
description: Flags breaks in the routine behind obsidian graph stats before a useful habit disappears.
value: Small habit gaps matter in note-taking systems because consistency usually drives the value more than occasional big sprints.
implementation: Capture a simple streak count or at least a last-activity timestamp during export.
visualization: Table of users by current streak and days since last activity.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Personal Knowledge & PKM — typical feeds: Obsidian graph stats (`obsidian:stats`), Roam daily notes (`roam:daily`), Logseq tasks (`logseq:task`), Zettelkasten notes (`zettel:note`), PKM review summaries (`pkm:review`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `obsidian:stats`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=obsidian:stats`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Obsidian graph stats, Roam daily notes, Logseq task exports, and Zettelkasten counts streamed to Splunk HEC via plugins, CSV exports, and scripted vault scans..

**Author notes:** Capture a simple streak count or at least a last-activity timestamp during export.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "obsidian:stats", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Obsidian Graph Stats Streak Gap Alert** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=obsidian:stats`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `days_since` (> 2) after latest, max — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `days_since`, `user`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats
| stats latest(streak_days) as streak_days, max(_time) as last_seen by user
| eval days_since=round((now()-last_seen)/86400,1)
| where days_since>2
| sort - days_since
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table days_since, user
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `days_since` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(days_since) AS p50 perc90(days_since) AS p90 perc99(days_since) AS p99 max(days_since) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.85.5: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Users By Current Streak And Days Since Last Activity (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `obsidian:stats` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=obsidian:stats | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
